statement: Latest published range for the integer DCCC in fetched sources is O'Bryant's k<=20 (arXiv math/0604347); Fornal-Sun arXiv 2607.24655 (Jul 2026) cites nothing beyond it. O'Bryant's k<=19 part is a week-long Mathematica search with no node counts, so not a certificate under our rules.

Minimal counterexample (least k, then least sum m_i) satisfies: 1<gcd<k; m_i | N=lcm pairwise gcds | lcm(1..k-1); every prime power dividing some m_i divides two m's; no m_i is a prime power; no prime divides all m_i; >=3 m's divisible by k-1 (if exactly 3, two more divisible by k-2); density sum 1/gcd(h_i,M)<=1 on every subfamily; for 7<=k<=30 each prime p>=k/2 divides 0 or exactly 2 m's. Also k>=7 (k<=6 excluded by O'Bryant sec 4.1, audited line by line; O'Bryant's unargued 'k>=5' remark closed via items 4',5,6). These are all constraints in O'Bryant Lemma 6; his Grow search (k<=19) uses only C1,C2,C4 and the density test with M=lcm of gcds.

O'Bryant Lemma 6 item 8, case k=30, l=3: the claim 'two of 17,19,23,29 lie in separate P_i' is unjustified; repaired: some large prime q!=p lies in some P_s, divides >=10 moduli, contradicting item 8's argument applied to q (needs >=10 disjoint nonempty subsets of 9 primes).
For k in {8,12,14,18,20,24,30}: if DCCC holds for all sizes <k then it holds for k. For 24 and 30 this is conditional on sizes 21,22,23 (not proved in fetched literature).
Group form: fetched sources (Zhu arXiv 0807.2207, Fornal-Sun 2607.24655) only give k=3,4 (plus finite p-groups, Sun 2006); no fetched source for k=5 as the cell claims.

Extend O'Bryant Lemma 6 item 8 beyond k=30: for 31<=k<=210 the omega-collision gives gcd>=210 when l>=4; find an argument for l=3 (three multiples of p>=k/2) to rule out k=32,38,42,44,48 (k-1 prime) conditionally on smaller k.

Write a certified (tools/cert.py, <10 min) search for k=21,22,23 using constraints C1-C7 (moduli divisors of lcm(1..k-1) with >=2 prime factors, no prime in all moduli, >=3 multiples of k-1, primes >=k/2 in exactly 0 or 2 moduli, subfamily density test); success makes k=24 decided.

Locate and check a proof of the group form for k=5 (cell claims known) and test whether O'Bryant's items 1-5 transfer to cosets (index-reduction replaces m_i/p by a supergroup of index n_i/p only when one exists).

O'Bryant Lemma 6 ends item 6 with 'this proves k>=5' without argument; closed: for k=4, item 5 gives >=3 multiples of 3; all 4 contradicts no-prime-divides-all (C4'), exactly 3 needs two more multiples of 2 among 1 remaining modulus.
